- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model frequently overcorrects in subsequent days; apply a “lag correction” by reducing forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the next 2–3 periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 77.00), model tends to hold too high; adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates the peak (especially after sentiment spike); cap forecast at 1–2% below the 30-day moving average of recent 10–15 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast with sentiment trend only if sentiment is >0.75 for 3+ consecutive days.
